prize_parts.citation: For the development of general, ligand-controlled palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: I have moved from B066 to B004. The chair asked whether PCET has a single attributable discovery, and after the first round I cannot honestly say it does: Meyer's concept, Mayer's thermochemistry and Hammes-Schiffer's theory are three strands of one field, Nocera's role is unsettled, and no other member supports it. My own test is a mechanism stated in physical terms and a method that made it usable. C-N coupling meets it: the problem is a specific elementary-step problem (amine binding, deprotonation, C-N reductive elimination competing with beta-hydride elimination and catalyst deactivation), and the answer was a ligand design that was tested mechanistically and reproduced independently for three decades. Buchwald and Hartwig built the catalytic, general version independently, which gives a clean pair and a short citation. It is mature, daily-used, and needs no argument about interpretation, which is the opposite of what I could say for B043 or B046.
statement.case_against: The 2010 cross-coupling prize is a real objection, and I do not dismiss it: a reader may see a new bond type for an honoured concept. I find Somfai's and Zou's answer persuasive but not conclusive, because it is an argument about mechanism that the committee must be able to state plainly in the citation. Kosugi and Migita's tin-amide coupling is a genuine precursor, and I am omitting Kosugi on the strength of colleagues' account of its stoichiometric tin reagents and narrow scope, not on a priority check of my own. The configuration also uses two names and one part, leaving a slot unused, and B040 has the larger effect on medicine if the committee can settle its credit.

responses.point: C-N coupling needed a different mechanistic solution from the 2010 C-C coupling prize (amine binding, deprotonation, C-N reductive elimination, suppression of beta-hydride elimination) and a new ligand toolbox, and Kosugi's tin-amide reaction was stoichiometric and narrow.
responses.response: This answers the point I raised in round 1. Separating the elementary-step problem from the C-C precedent is what a physical-organic reading wants, and it is what makes the ligand work the discovery and not a corollary. On Kosugi, I accept the distinction between a stoichiometric tin reaction with limited scope and a general catalytic method, but I ask that the citation say 'general, ligand-controlled catalytic' so that the wording itself protects against a priority challenge. With that wording I will leave him out and mention him only as a precursor in the committee's record. This is why B004 is now my first choice.

responses.point: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a decisive piece of pKa-tuned physical-organic design, with the in vivo outcome set by the SNALP and ionizable-lipid optimisation (Cullis, MacLachlan, Anderson) more than by the earliest liposome formulation.
responses.response: I agree that the pKa tuning is real physical chemistry and that the consequences are the largest on the list. What I cannot get past is that your trio rests on a judgement about which step counts as decisive, and Chabes, Zou and Somfai each defend a different trio. Hope and Madden's remote-loading and early formulation work, MacLachlan's ionizable lipid and Anderson's lipidoids are separate contributions, and the 2023 Medicine overlap adds a second risk. I would take B040 if the committee can settle on a defensible three from the primary literature, which is why it is my first alternative. Until then a clean pair is the lower risk, and I do not see that as a judgement against the science.

responses.point: Car-Parrinello has one idea, a clean two-author credit and four decades of independent adoption, and the chair asks whether Brzezinski should move toward B040 or B004.
responses.response: I take the attribution argument seriously, and I have moved toward B004 as you ask, because my own B066 does not have a single attributable discovery. On B021 I remain where I was in round 1: I want to know what chemistry it unlocked beyond the original method, and the answer given in this round is mostly its descendants and its specialist users. I also note the 2013 and 2024 computational prizes, which add a recency question that B004 does not carry. I do not think theory should be penalised for being theory, but I would not put B021 ahead of a method that is used daily at the bench.

responses.point: PCET credit is split across theory, thermochemistry and electrocatalysis with Nocera unresolved, so the citation would be diffuse, and the evidence for concerted versus stepwise pathways would need to be as decisive across systems as C-N coupling is across substrates.
responses.response: That is a fair test and I did not meet it. In respiratory enzymes the concerted-versus-stepwise question is still handled system by system, and the field has no one experiment or theory that the whole community accepts as the founding result. My round-1 reasoning that Nocera's work was mainly demonstration was also a judgement I could not support from the supplied credit. I withdraw B066 as a first choice for this year and keep it only as an alternative, and I note that my field proximity was the reason to be more sceptical, not less.

responses.point: B046 rests on induced proximity as one principle, and the cereblon mechanism has been reproduced independently, but no designed PROTAC is approved and Chabes proposes B029 as a fallback.
responses.response: I accept that the cereblon identification is a mechanism result with strong independent support. My difficulty is the one you name yourself: PROTAC invention and cereblon discovery are different findings by different people, and a three-name cap leaves out Sakamoto, Ito, Ciulli and Gray. A citation stitched across two lineages invites the objection that the committee has merged two prizes. I would rather the committee wait for the field to settle, and I regard B004 as the better-founded choice for this year.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat Pd C-N coupling as distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize or as an extension of it.
Kosugi's priority: I have not seen the expert report and rely on colleagues' account that the tin-amide reaction was stoichiometric and narrow.
Whether the ionizable-lipid credit for B040 can be settled on a defensible trio, which would change my ranking of it.
Whether I have discounted PCET too far because it is close to my own field, in either direction.
statement.conflict_note: No personal or institutional connection to Buchwald, Hartwig or Kosugi, or to any other shortlisted candidate. PCET (B066) lies close to my own research in biological energy conversion and I have moved away from it as a first choice, partly to guard against that bias. Xiaodong Zou is a Stockholm University colleague but is not a candidate and is not in my configuration.
